newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX index at record levels as bourse opens.
newsitem.headline: German DAX index at record levels as bourse opens.

text.p: German shares advance strongly in early bourse trade to further record highs, lifted by the dollar penetrating the 1.66-mark threshold and underpinned by overnight Wall Street gains.

The 30-share DAX index of German blue-chips was up 31.48 points, or 1.01 percent, at 3,135.62 points in early floor trade, trading around heady record heights which traders said showed no signs of letting up, traders said.

"The market is a bit nervous this morning but still wants to keep going higher," said one Frankfurt trader. "We are seriously searching for direction and one cannot rule out a correction after such healthy gains."

A surging dollar, tied to German Finance Minister Theo Waigel's comments that it would be pointless to set foreign exchange targets at upcoming G7 finance minister summit in Berlin, and stable German debt market were main factors pushing stocks higher.
Traders were also focusing on the 1330 GMT release of U.S. jobless data for January, which could have an unsettling effect, dealers said.
The big corporate news early on was confirmation that the diversified utility Veba AG had ended its telecommunications alliance with Britain's Cable & Wireless.
Veba shares were up 80 pfennigs at 92.30 marks after saying C&W would sell its 45 percent stake in Vebacom for 2.21 billion marks, and buy out Veba's half of C&W Europe SA for 90 million.
Traders said Veba, which will also hold on to its 10.4 percent stake in C&W, paid a fair price to buy out C&W but were unsure to predict an outlook for Veba shares.
Siemens AG was among the volume leaders in floor trade, rising 2.83 marks to 85.73 marks after Bayerische Vereinsbank and Dresdner Bank raised their ratings on the Munich-based electronics group.
